summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dyspnea, chest pain, and hypoglycemia, following a recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. Evaluation revealed a new moderate pericardial effusion and small pleural effusions on CT, with echocardiography confirming no cardiac tamponade. The effusion was attributed to likely uremic pericarditis in the setting of ESRD and peritoneal dialysis. She was treated with aspirin per cardiology, and antibiotics were discontinued after infection was ruled out. Pain management was optimized with a stepwise regimen avoiding Dilaudid due to its exacerbation of gastroparesis. Her condition stabilized, she was discharged home with instructions to continue peritoneal dialysis, monitor symptoms, and follow up for a repeat echocardiogram in one week.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
